posts.headline: He found a newborn left in a forest. Today *35 daughters* call him Baba
posts.body: Hare Ram Pandey and his wife Bhavani Kumari run Narayan Sewa Ashram in Deoghar, Jharkhand, a home for girls abandoned in forests, bushes and trains. Now police and hospitals call him whenever they find an abandoned child.
posts.source: The Better India, The Logical Indian, ThePrint
posts.caption:
On 9 December 2004, Hare Ram Pandey found a newborn girl abandoned in a Jharkhand forest, barely breathing. 💛

That moment changed his life. With his wife, Bhavani Kumari, he started Narayan Sewa Ashram in Deoghar, a home for girls left in forests, bushes and trains. Today 35 girls call him Baba, and police and hospitals call him whenever they find an abandoned child.

Not every hero wears a uniform. Some just say yes, again and again. 🙏

Tag someone who believes every child deserves a family 👇

Sources: The Better India, The Logical Indian, ThePrint

posts.sub: Feeding India's Unboxing Joy brought toys, books and learning kits to children before Children's Day.

slides.title: An annual *gift-donation drive* by Feeding India
slides.body: Run by Feeding India (Eternal Foundation) at schools and learning centres in its Daily Feeding Program.

slides.title: Dolls, puzzles, STEM kits and *books*
slides.body: 13 brand partners joined in, including Mattel, Penguin Random House, Funskool and Smartivity.

slides.body: Feeding India works with 2,000+ schools and anganwadis across 157 districts (FY 2025-26).

posts.takeaway: Play builds *confidence and curiosity*. Every child deserves both.
posts.source: India CSR; Feeding India Annual Report 2025-26
posts.caption:
1.1 lakh children. One box of joy each. 🎁

Ahead of Children's Day, Feeding India by Eternal Foundation ran its annual Unboxing Joy drive, bringing dolls, puzzles, clay, STEM kits, craft kits and books to more than 1.1 lakh children in over 140 districts, with 13 brand partners. The children are part of Feeding India's Daily Feeding Program, which serves meals to about 1.7 lakh children every day.

posts.stat_label: of Bisleri water (GO 270, made in Goa, Sept 2025) under an FSSAI sale ban
posts.headline: Bisleri & FSSAI: *what you need to know*
points: FSSAI: one sample failed the bromate limit, then a PAH test; it has sanctioned prosecution
Bisleri: none of that batch is on sale now; all 143 plants are running
Tip: check the batch number printed on your bottle
posts.source: The Week, ThePrint (PTI), Food Safety Helpline
posts.caption:
Is your packaged water safe? Here's what happened, in simple words. 💧

FSSAI said one sample of Bisleri packaged drinking water failed the bromate limit and, on further testing, a PAH test. It has sanctioned prosecution and ordered a sale ban on that one batch, GO 270, made in Goa in September 2025, and asked Bisleri to find the root cause.

Bisleri says it makes more than 50,000 batches a year, none of this batch is in the market now, and all 143 of its plants are running. It says a re-test found bromate within the permissible limit. The matter is now with the authorities.

What is bromate? It can form when water is disinfected with ozone. India's limit for packaged drinking water is 0.01 mg per litre.

Tip: the batch number is printed on every bottle. 👀

Save this and share it with your family 🔖

Sources: The Week, ThePrint (PTI), Food Safety Helpline

posts.headline: Water was 2 km away. Now it *comes to their fields*
posts.sub: How 10 shared solar pumps changed farming in Tulyachapada, a tribal hamlet in Palghar, Maharashtra.

slides.title: A dam nearby, but *dry fields*
slides.body: Tulyachapada in Mokhada sits near the Morchondi dam, yet about 60% of farmers left for work after the monsoon.

slides.stat_label: shared solar pumps and a 10-km pipeline
slides.title: Groups of *10 farmers* share each pump
slides.body: Pragati Pratishthan worked with farmers, Gram Oorja built it, and CSR support covered their share.

slides.title: More crops, *fewer people leaving*
slides.body: Farm income rose from ₹18.3 lakh (2021) to ₹31.1 lakh (2024). Gram Oorja says migration fell 90%.

posts.takeaway: "Now the water comes to me." When water reaches the field, *families can stay*.
posts.caption:
Water was 2 km away. Now it comes to their fields. ☀️💧

Tulyachapada, a tribal hamlet in Palghar's Mokhada block, sits near the Morchondi dam, yet farmers struggled to get water to their land and many migrated for work after the monsoon. Since 2019, 10 shared solar pumps and a 10-km pipeline, set up by Pragati Pratishthan and Gram Oorja with CSR support from Bank of America, have changed that.

Farmed land grew from 4-5 acres to about 96 acres, farm income rose from ₹18.3 lakh in 2021 to ₹31.1 lakh in 2024, and Gram Oorja says migration has fallen by 90%.

"Now the water comes to me," says farmer Pandurang Lahare. 🌱
